The search turned up several 2026 reports on nested and child sessions. The most prominent is a desktop feature, while the rest are community blogs, skill pages, and bug reports, so treat the details as unverified against Anthropic's own documentation.

- **Desktop nested sessions (October 2026):** One blog reports that Anthropic updated the Claude Code desktop app on October 14, 2026. Nested sessions are child sessions that Claude Code opens on its own when asked to run several tasks in parallel, one per task. Each child session works independently and, once done, reports its result back to the main session. A second blog says Claude only sees sessions the desktop app runs itself: local, SSH, and WSL sessions in the Code tab. Cloud sessions, CLI sessions, and VS Code sessions are invisible to this surface.
- **Cost and context:** That same blog says every session, including every child session, loads its own startup context. Spin up five nested sessions and you pay that startup cost five times.
- **Spawning from the CLI:** A community skill page describes launching child Claude Code processes via subprocess, which requires clearing the nesting env vars. It recommends a fan-out pattern for parallel work, and says each child gets its own context window, tool access, and session, unlike Task-tool subagents.
- **Known limitations (GitHub/claudeissues reports):**
  - A cloud session lineage depth limit of 8 was reported on 2026-09-28. The same session, spawning children side by side, created 9 without a refusal.
  - Subagents spawned by general-purpose agents were reported as invisible and uncontrollable by both the parent session and the user.
  - A May 2026 issue reports that the filtering is at the harness layer, so sub-agents can't spawn other sub-agents, and the report says "No, this never worked".
  - A May 2026 request asks for a way for a parent to be notified when a child session ends or goes idle, since no such mechanism existed then.
- **Nesting detection:** A March 2026 issue reported that the CLAUDECODE and CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT environment variables cause the child process to refuse to launch when spawned from inside a session. It was marked resolved on March 13, 2026.

Gaps: I did not find official Anthropic documentation for these features, and the desktop-feature details come from secondary blogs. Check the Claude Code docs or changelog before relying on specifics.

content.content:
The documentation doesn't use the term "nested sessions." It describes three ways to start background sessions, plus how subagents relate to them.

## Starting a background session from the shell

Pass `--bg` (or `--background`) with a prompt. The prompt is a positional argument, not a `-p` value.

```bash
claude --bg "investigate the flaky SettingsChangeDetector test"
```

Requirements and rules:

- **Don't combine with `-p` or `--print`.** Claude Code rejects this before creating a session.
- **Put the flag first**, as in `claude --bg "<prompt>"`. A prompt that mentions `--bg` is delivered as typed only when the flag comes first. If the position is ambiguous (for example, after a run of combined short flags), Claude Code exits with `Couldn't tell whether --bg is a flag or text here` and starts nothing.
- **Untrusted directories:** the workspace trust dialog appears first. In a script with no dialog, the command fails with `Workspace not trusted`.

Optional flags:

```bash
# Set a display name
claude --bg --name "flaky-test-fix" "investigate the flaky SettingsChangeDetector test"

# Run a specific defined subagent as the main agent
claude --agent code-reviewer --bg "address review comments on PR 1234"

# Continue an existing conversation under its full session ID
claude --resume 1f0e2c9a-6d0b-4c11-9f39-2a77c1d4e8b5 --bg "pick up where you left off"

# Start a copy instead of continuing in place
claude --resume <id> --bg --fork-session "..."

# Run a shell command as a background job (no Claude session, no model)
claude --bg --exec 'pytest -x'
```

`--continue`, a bare `--resume`, or `--resume` with a name or path always starts a copy under a new ID. If the `--agent` name doesn't exist, the session exits with `--agent '<name>' not found`.

After starting, Claude prints the short ID and management commands:

```text
backgrounded · 7c5dcf5d · flaky-test-fix
  claude agents             list sessions
  claude attach 7c5dcf5d    open in this terminal
  claude logs 7c5dcf5d      show recent output
  claude stop 7c5dcf5d      stop this session
```

## Spawning from an existing session

- **`/background` or `/bg [prompt]`** moves the current conversation to a background session and frees your terminal. An optional prompt adds one more instruction first.
- **`/fork [prompt]`** copies the current conversation into a new background session while the original keeps running. Without a prompt, the copy waits for input. Send one with `Space` in agent view or with `claude attach <id>`.
- **`←` on an empty prompt** backgrounds the current session and opens agent view.

## Dispatching from agent view

Type a prompt in the dispatch input and press `Enter`. Prefixes control startup:

| Input | Effect |
| :- | :- |
| `<agent-name> <prompt>` or `@<agent-name>` | Runs a custom subagent as the session's main agent |
| `@<repo>` | Runs the session in a child repository (one level below the launch directory) |
| `! <command>` | Starts a shell job instead of a Claude session |
| `/model`, `/effort`, `/fast` | Sets the defaults for sessions dispatched afterward (not sent as prompts) |

## Subagents and teammates

Subagents and teammates a session spawns don't appear as separate rows. A subagent you spawn inside a session inherits its working directory, unless it sets `isolation: worktree`.

## Notes on configuration flags

- `claude agents` accepts `--settings`, `--setting-sources`, `--plugin-dir`, `--add-dir`, and `--mcp-config`. Place `--add-dir` and `--mcp-config` after `agents`, or `claude agents --json` fails with `unknown option`.
- Pass repeated values as separate flags, such as `--add-dir a --add-dir b`. The space-separated form isn't supported.

The page doesn't document invoking `claude --bg` from inside a running session's Bash tool. If you need that, verify the behavior directly.

input.message:
**No formal "nested sessions" feature in official Claude Code docs.** 

What exists instead:

1. **Background sessions** (official, documented):
   - **Command:** `claude --bg "<prompt>"` from shell, or `/bg [prompt]` / `/fork [prompt]` from within a session
   - **Invocation:** Slash commands or CLI flag; no setting/gate required
   - **Visibility:** Each spawned session gets its own ID; list with `claude agents`; watch with `claude attach <id>` or `claude logs <id>`
   - **Scope:** Full independent sessions, not subagents

2. **Desktop "nested sessions" (internal term, October 2026 feature)**:
   - Anthropic's desktop app auto-spawns child sessions for parallel tasks; each is independent and reports results to parent
   - **Limitation:** Only visible in Claude Code desktop (not CLI, VS Code, or cloud sessions)
   - **Cost:** Each child session loads full startup context

3. **Known limits:**
   - Cloud sessions have a lineage depth limit of ~8
   - Subagents (spawned via Agent/Task tools) cannot spawn other subagents
   - Nesting env vars (`CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`) previously blocked spawning; marked resolved March 2026

**Sources:**
- [Claude Code agent-view.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view.md)
- [Search: Claude Code desktop nested sessions October 2026](https://pasqualepillitteri.it/en/news/24032/claude-code-desktop-nested-sessions-environments)
- [GitHub issue: Session spawning context passing](https://claudeissues.com/issue/67379-session-spawning-allow-a-session-to-spin-off-a-child-session-with-passed-context)
